artists.biography: Jesus Jones are a British alternative dance band. The Wiltshire-based group, formed in late 1988, recorded and performed in the late 1980s, throughout the 1990s, and into the 2000s. They are best remembered for their track, "Right Here, Right Now", an international hit and subsequently globally appropriated for promotional and advertising campaigns. They are also well-remembered for the songs "Real Real Real" and "International Bright Young Thing."

perplexity.description:
Released in January 1991 on Food Records (not Demon Records), Doubt is the second studio album by British rock band Jesus Jones. The album marked a significant evolution in the band’s sound, blending electronic textures with guitar-driven alternative rock to create a style often described as alternative dance. Drawing from the energy of their debut Liquidizer, Doubt refined their approach with tighter songwriting and a more accessible pop sensibility, while still retaining the band’s signature use of samples, loops, and dance rhythms. Frontman Mike Edwards led the creative direction, with most songs written and produced by him, resulting in a cohesive and energetic record that captured the spirit of the early 1990s UK alternative scene.

Doubt stands as a pivotal release in Jesus Jones’ discography, cementing their commercial success and broadening their international appeal. The album topped the UK charts and reached #25 in the US, fueled by hit singles like “International Bright Young Thing,” “Real Real Real,” and “Right Here, Right Now,” which became an anthem of the era. Critics noted the album’s unevenness but praised its infectious energy and innovative fusion of rock and electronic elements. Its rapid recording process—completed in just a week—reflected the band’s momentum and confidence, making Doubt a defining work of the early 1990s alternative dance movement.
